entities.name: John Watts Jr.
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
John Watts Jr. (1749–1836) was an American Federalist politician from New York who served in the U.S. House of Representatives (1793–1795) and as a judge of the New York Supreme Court. A member of a prominent colonial New York family — his father John Watts Sr. had been a loyalist during the Revolution — Watts Jr. navigated the difficult transition from colonial elite to republican citizen, aligning with the Federalist tradition that best preserved the social world of New York's commercial establishment.

His brief congressional service coincided with the establishment of the Jay Treaty negotiations — his fellow New Yorker John Jay was negotiating the treaty with Britain that would provoke intense controversy — and with Hamilton's Treasury system at its height.

New York's Federalist elite — the merchants, lawyers, and landowners who had supported the Constitution's ratification at Poughkeepsie in 1788 — was the social world within which Watts moved.

His long life (1749–1836) spanned from colonial New York to the Jacksonian era.
